# Plan and Implement

## Change Summary

Core geometry scaling logic (filter flow, heater power, plant biomass, auto-stocking, microbe scaling) was already fully implemented with named constants and documented formulas in tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs. This execution adds the remaining test coverage required by the acceptance criteria: (1) a combined 100L acceptance test verifying filter ~1000 lph, heater ~75W, and plant biomass ~15g together; (2) light intensity independence from tank size; (3) substrate depth independence from tank size; (4) aeration effect scaling via habitat registry; (5) integration test proving a mismatched filter (large tank, tiny filter media) produces worse cycling balance (higher nitrite) than the auto-scaled version; (6) three-size comparison (20L/60L/200L) showing proportionally scaled tanks cycle similarly. All 16 unit tests and 4 integration tests pass. Clippy and fmt are clean.

## Steps

1. [Completed] Reviewed existing implementation in tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs: scaling constants (FILTER_FLOW_TURNOVERS_PER_HOUR=10, HEATER_WATTS_PER_LITER=0.75, PLANT_BIOMASS_G_PER_1000_CM2_FOOTPRINT=3.0, AUTO_STOCK_ADULTS_PER_LITER=0.2), scale_hardware_to_geometry() function, and apply_startup_overrides() priority system. All core scaling logic confirmed complete.
2. [Completed] Added unit test combined_100l_scaling_produces_expected_hardware_and_biomass to geometry_scaling.rs: verifies 100L tank gets filter ~1000 lph, heater ~75W, and total plant biomass ~15g (2 guilds) in a single test.
3. [Completed] Added unit test light_intensity_independent_of_tank_size: verifies intensity_index and photoperiod_hours are identical across 1×, 2×, and nano scales (fixture property, not tank-scaled).
4. [Completed] Added unit test substrate_depth_independent_of_tank_size: verifies each substrate layer depth_cm is identical between 1× and 2× geometry despite 4× footprint difference.
5. [Completed] Added unit test aeration_effect_scales_via_habitat_registry: verifies aeration intensity setting is fixture-level (identical across scales), but colonizable area (which mediates physical aeration effect) scales ~4× with 2× geometry.
6. [Completed] Added integration test mismatched_filter_shows_worse_cycling: 2× geometry with auto-scaled filter vs 2× geometry with 200cm² tiny filter. Tiny filter produces higher nitrite (imbalanced nitrogen pipeline where AOB outpaces NOB) — proves scaling rules prevent mismatch.
7. [Completed] Added integration test nano_vs_standard_vs_large_similar_cycling: three sizes (~20L, ~60L, ~200L) using same base scenario (medium_planted) at different geometry scales with proportional feeding. All three pass common envelope and show biofilter maturity within 5× ratio.
8. [Completed] Ran cargo test (all pass except pre-existing nano_cycle_baseline_envelope NO3 issue), cargo clippy -- -D warnings (clean), cargo fmt (clean).

## Validation Evidence

- 16/16 geometry_scaling unit tests pass including 4 new tests (combined_100l, light_independence, substrate_depth, aeration_scaling)
- 4/4 e2e_geometry_scaling integration tests pass including 2 new tests (mismatched_filter, nano_vs_standard_vs_large)
- 11/11 materialization tests pass (unchanged)
- 5/5 startup_overrides tests pass (unchanged)
- cargo clippy -- -D warnings produces zero warnings
- cargo fmt --check produces no diffs
- Pre-existing nano_cycle_baseline_envelope failure (NO3 0.23 outside [0.5, 3.0]) confirmed unrelated to changes (same failure on stashed baseline)

## Outstanding Risks

- Pre-existing nano_cycle_baseline_envelope test failure (NO3 below expected floor) is unrelated to geometry scaling but may need attention in a separate bead.
- The mismatched-filter integration test demonstrates cycling balance degradation via nitrite rather than TAN, because bacteria colonize all surfaces (not just filter media). This is model-faithful but differs from naive expectation that TAN would be dramatically worse. The test documents actual model behavior.
- The three-size comparison uses a generous 5× maturity ratio tolerance because different geometry scales produce different substrate-displacement ratios (fixed substrate depth displaces a larger fraction of volume in smaller tanks). Tightening to 20% would require substrate depth to scale with geometry.
